tools.name: automation_create_workflow
tools.description:
Create a new visual automation workflow with unique immutable slug. Generates visual canvas representation with nodes/connections and executable JSON. Supports 4 trigger types (manual, schedule, webhook, event) and 594 available tools. Returns automation_id, slug, and visual_flow_json for canvas rendering.

Slug format: wf_<8random>_<timestamp> (auto-generated, immutable). Use slug for all workflow operations.

USE CASES:
1. Email automation - Daily digest of unread emails with AI summaries
2. Data pipelines - Hourly sync of Shopify orders to Google Sheets
3. Smart notifications - Slack alerts for high-priority emails only
4. Report generation - Weekly sales reports with charts via email
5. CRM workflows - Follow-up emails for inactive clients

WHEN TO USE:
User requests NEW workflow (not modifying existing). User describes sequence of actions with trigger. User wants visual representation. User needs to automate repetitive tasks.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
User wants to modify EXISTING workflow → use automation_update_workflow. User wants one-time execution → use automation_execute_workflow. User wants to change schedule only → use automation_schedule_workflow. Workflow has 20+ actions → recommend breaking into sub-workflows.

WORKFLOW:
1. Analyze user request → identify trigger and actions
2. Map user intent to tool names from 594-tool library
3. Construct actions array with parameters and {{placeholders}}
4. Call automation_create_workflow(title, actions, trigger, category)
5. Explain created workflow to user with slug
6. Offer to schedule/execute/open in canvas

BEST PRACTICES:
Use descriptive titles (visible in UI). Keep actions sequential (avoid complex branching). Use {{placeholders}} for data flow between steps. Set appropriate category for organization. Always explain slug to user (unique identifier). Validate tool names before creating. Test with automation_execute_workflow before scheduling.

ERROR HANDLING:
Invalid tool name → Fetch tool list with list_platform_tools. Missing required parameter → Check tool schema with get_tool_schema. Invalid cron expression → Validate with cron syntax guide. Placeholder not found → Check previous action outputs. Trigger type not supported → Limit to: manual, schedule, webhook, event.

RELATED TOOLS:
automation_schedule_workflow - Activate created workflow with cron schedule
automation_execute_workflow - Test workflow with sample data before scheduling
automation_update_workflow - Modify workflow after creation (add/remove actions)
automation_open_workflow_in_canvas - Show visual representation in UI
automation_publish_workflow - Move draft workflow to production execution
automation_get_workflow_by_slug - Retrieve workflow details by slug

tools.name: automation_update_workflow
tools.description:
Update existing workflow by slug - add/remove actions, modify trigger, change parameters. UI automatically refreshes canvas after update. Requires workflow slug (wf_<8random>_<timestamp>).

OPERATIONS:
add_actions - Append or insert actions at specific position
remove_actions - Remove actions by position array [0, 2]
update_trigger - Change trigger type or schedule
update_action_parameters - Modify parameters of existing action
update_metadata - Change title or description

USE CASES:
1. Add notification step - Append email/Slack action after processing
2. Fix parameters - Update max_results, email addresses, spreadsheet IDs
3. Change schedule - Modify cron from daily to hourly
4. Remove step - Delete action that's no longer needed
5. Insert action - Add step between existing actions

WHEN TO USE:
User requests modification to EXISTING workflow with slug. User says 'add step', 'remove action', 'change schedule', 'update parameters'. User references workflow by slug (wf_xxx).

WHEN NOT TO USE:
User wants to create NEW workflow → use automation_create_workflow. User doesn't have workflow slug → use automation_list_workflows to find it. User wants to schedule existing workflow → use automation_schedule_workflow.

WORKFLOW:
1. Get workflow slug from user or thread context
2. Determine update type (add/remove/update)
3. Call automation_update_workflow with operation parameters
4. Confirm changes to user with specific details
5. Note UI canvas auto-refreshes (no manual reload needed)
6. If scheduled, show next run time

BEST PRACTICES:
Always get current workflow state first with automation_get_workflow. Validate tool names before adding actions. Use position parameter to insert (not append). Merge parameters when updating (don't replace all). Explain changes clearly to user. Test updated workflow with automation_execute_workflow.

ERROR HANDLING:
Invalid slug → Use automation_list_workflows to find correct slug. Invalid position → Check workflow has that many actions. Invalid tool name → Use list_platform_tools to verify. Missing required parameters → Use get_tool_schema to see requirements. Trigger conflict → Validate new schedule doesn't overlap.

RELATED TOOLS:
automation_get_workflow - Get current workflow state before updating
automation_create_workflow - Create new workflow instead of updating
automation_schedule_workflow - Change schedule without full update
automation_execute_workflow - Test updated workflow before scheduling
automation_list_workflows - Find workflow slug if user doesn't have it
automation_open_workflow_in_canvas - Show updated workflow visually

tools.name: automation_list_workflows
tools.description:
List all saved automation workflows with metadata, status, execution counts. Filter by category or status. Default returns 50 most recent workflows. Response includes automation_id, slug, title, status, category, trigger_type, action_count, execution_count, last_run timestamp, created_at. Use slug from results for operations (execute, schedule, update).

USE CASES:
1. Workflow inventory - Show user all their automations
2. Find workflow - User remembers title, needs slug
3. Filter workflows - Show only email or active workflows
4. Workflow management - List before selecting one to modify
5. Status overview - Quick view of what's running

WHEN TO USE:
User asks 'show my workflows', 'list automations', 'what workflows exist?', 'find email workflow'. User needs workflow slug for other operations. User wants overview of all automations.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
User wants details of specific workflow → use automation_get_workflow. User wants execution history → use automation_get_execution_history. User wants to create workflow → use automation_create_workflow.

WORKFLOW:
1. Determine if user wants filtered list (category, status, limit)
2. Call automation_list_workflows with filters
3. Format results clearly with numbers
4. Show key info: title, slug, trigger, last run, status
5. Offer next actions (execute, view details, modify)

BEST PRACTICES:
Show most recently updated first. Include execution counts for context. Highlight active vs inactive workflows. Use slug for subsequent operations. Filter by category to narrow results. Show clear formatting with numbers.

ERROR HANDLING:
No workflows found → Suggest creating first workflow. Empty filtered results → Try different filter or show all. Invalid category → List valid categories. Invalid status → Use draft/active/inactive/all only.

tools.name: automation_execute_workflow
tools.description:
Execute workflow immediately with manual trigger. Returns execution ID for progress tracking. Validates workflow, resolves placeholders ({{user_input}}, {{date}}, {{timestamp}}), executes actions sequentially, and returns status with step results.

Execution flow: Validate → Resolve placeholders → Execute actions → Each step output available to next step as {{previous_output}} → Return final status (success/failure).

USE CASES:
1. Test new workflow - Verify workflow works before scheduling
2. One-time task - Run workflow once with specific input data
3. Debug workflow - Execute to see which step fails
4. Manual trigger - User wants to run workflow on demand
5. Input data workflow - Pass dynamic data via {{user_input}} placeholders

WHEN TO USE:
User says 'run this workflow', 'execute automation', 'test now', 'try this workflow'. Testing before scheduling. One-time execution with specific data. Debugging workflow failures.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
User wants recurring execution → use automation_schedule_workflow. User wants to create AND execute → use automation_create_workflow then execute. User wants execution history → use automation_get_execution_history.

WORKFLOW:
1. Get workflow slug from user or thread context
2. Prepare input_data if workflow uses {{user_input}} placeholders
3. Link to thread_id if executing in conversation
4. Call automation_execute_workflow
5. Show execution progress with step results
6. Explain final status and any errors

BEST PRACTICES:
Always test new workflows before scheduling. Provide input_data for {{user_input}} placeholders. Link executions to thread for context. Show step-by-step progress to user. Explain errors and suggest fixes. Use execution_id to check status later.

ERROR HANDLING:
Workflow not found → Use automation_list_workflows to find slug. Step fails → Show error details and suggest fixes. Missing credentials → Check platform authentication. Invalid parameters → Verify tool requirements with get_tool_schema. Placeholder not resolved → Check previous step outputs.

tools.name: automation_schedule_workflow
tools.description:
Schedule workflow for automatic execution at specified times using cron expressions. Activates workflow and creates background scheduler task. Supports timezone configuration (default: UTC). Validates cron syntax and calculates next run time.

Cron patterns: '0 9 * * *' (daily 9am), '0 */2 * * *' (every 2 hours), '*/15 * * * *' (every 15 min), '0 9 * * 1' (Monday 9am), '0 0 1 * *' (monthly 1st day).

USE CASES:
1. Daily reports - Email summary every morning at 9am
2. Hourly data sync - Sync orders to sheets every hour
3. Weekly summaries - Send report every Monday
4. Monthly tasks - Generate invoices first day of month
5. Frequent checks - Monitor API every 15 minutes

WHEN TO USE:
User says 'schedule this workflow', 'run every hour', 'activate automation', 'set up recurring execution'. User has created workflow and wants automatic execution.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
User wants one-time execution → use automation_execute_workflow. User wants to create AND schedule → use automation_create_workflow with schedule trigger. User wants to change existing schedule → use automation_update_workflow with update_trigger.

WORKFLOW:
1. Verify workflow exists with automation_get_workflow
2. Determine cron pattern from user intent
3. Set timezone if user specifies (default UTC)
4. Call automation_schedule_workflow
5. Calculate and show next run time to user
6. Explain recurring pattern clearly

BEST PRACTICES:
Test workflow with automation_execute_workflow before scheduling. Use UTC timezone unless user specifies location. Validate cron expression before calling. Calculate next run time and show user. Explain recurring pattern in plain language. Monitor first few executions with automation_get_execution_history.

ERROR HANDLING:
Invalid cron expression → Show cron pattern guide and correct syntax. Workflow not found → Use automation_list_workflows to find slug. Already scheduled → Suggest automation_update_workflow to change schedule. Timezone invalid → List valid timezone names. Workflow has no actions → Cannot schedule empty workflow.

RELATED TOOLS:
automation_create_workflow - Create workflow with schedule trigger (alternative)
automation_execute_workflow - Test workflow before scheduling
automation_deactivate_workflow - Pause scheduled workflow temporarily
automation_update_workflow - Change schedule without deactivating
automation_get_execution_history - Monitor scheduled executions
automation_get_workflow_status - Check if workflow is scheduled

Complex - Schedule with timezone (every 2 hours in Sydney)

tools.name: automation_deactivate_workflow
tools.description:
Deactivate a scheduled workflow. Stops automatic execution but preserves the workflow.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this when user says 'pause this workflow', 'stop the automation', 'deactivate this'
- Stops scheduled execution immediately
- Workflow remains in database (can be reactivated later)
- Does NOT delete workflow or execution history
- Status changes from 'active' to 'inactive'

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'Your Daily Gmail Summary workflow has been deactivated.

⏸️ Status: Inactive
📊 Total executions: 45 (95.6% success)
🕐 Last run: 2 hours ago (success)

The workflow is paused and won't run automatically. You can:
- Reactivate it with automation_schedule_workflow()
- Run it manually with automation_execute_workflow()
- Delete it permanently with automation_delete_workflow()'

COMMON USE CASES:
- User wants to pause workflow temporarily
- Workflow needs modifications before next run
- Testing period is over
- User is away and doesn't need automated runs

REACTIVATION:
- Call automation_schedule_workflow() with same cron to reactivate
- All workflow settings and history are preserved

tools.name: automation_delete_workflow
tools.description:
Delete a workflow permanently. This cannot be undone.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this when user says 'delete this workflow', 'remove the automation', 'I don't need this anymore'
- PERMANENT deletion - cannot be recovered
- Removes workflow, execution history, and scheduler tasks
- Ask for confirmation before executing (this is destructive)

CONFIRMATION PATTERN:
1. User requests deletion
2. AI responds: 'Are you sure you want to delete [Workflow Title] (wf_xxx)? This will:
   - Delete the workflow permanently
   - Remove all execution history (X runs)
   - Stop any scheduled executions
   
   This cannot be undone. Reply "yes delete" to confirm.'
3. User confirms
4. AI executes automation_delete_workflow()

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'Your Daily Gmail Summary workflow (wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847) has been deleted permanently.

🗑️ Removed:
- Workflow configuration
- 45 execution records
- Scheduled task (daily at 9:00 AM)

The workflow cannot be recovered. If you need similar functionality, you can create a new workflow.'

ALTERNATIVE SUGGESTION:
- If user might need workflow later, suggest automation_deactivate_workflow() instead
- Deactivation preserves workflow for future reactivation
- Deletion is only for workflows user is certain they won't use again

WARNING:
- Always confirm before deleting
- Explain what will be lost (execution history, schedule)
- Suggest export with automation_export_workflow() for backup

tools.name: automation_get_execution_history
tools.description:
Get execution history for workflow showing past runs with timestamps, status, duration, and errors. Returns chronological list with detailed step results. Filter by status (success/failure/running) for debugging. Default limit 20 executions (configurable).

Response includes: execution_id, started_at, completed_at, duration_seconds, status, steps array (tool, parameters, output, duration), error message, trigger_type (manual/schedule/webhook/event).

USE CASES:
1. Monitor workflow health - Check success rate and recent failures
2. Debug failures - Filter status='failure' to see error patterns
3. Performance analysis - Review duration trends across executions
4. Audit trail - Track when workflow ran and what it did
5. Troubleshooting - Identify which step fails consistently

WHEN TO USE:
User asks 'how is workflow doing?', 'show execution history', 'when did it last run?', 'did it fail?', 'why isn't it working?'. Debugging workflow issues. Monitoring scheduled workflow performance. Checking if workflow executed.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
User wants to execute workflow → use automation_execute_workflow. User wants workflow details (not history) → use automation_get_workflow. User wants to create/modify workflow → use create or update tools.

WORKFLOW:
1. Get workflow slug from user or context
2. Determine if user needs all history or filtered (failures only)
3. Set appropriate limit (default 20, or specific count)
4. Call automation_get_execution_history
5. Calculate success rate from results
6. Show formatted history with status icons
7. If failures found, analyze errors and suggest fixes

BEST PRACTICES:
Always calculate success rate for user. Show most recent executions first. Filter by status='failure' when debugging. Analyze error patterns (API limits, credentials, parameters). Suggest fixes based on common errors. Use execution_id to reference specific runs.

ERROR HANDLING:
Workflow not found → Use automation_list_workflows to find slug. No execution history → Workflow never executed. Invalid status filter → Use success/failure/running/all only. Empty results with filter → No executions match status.

RELATED TOOLS:

automation_get_workflow - Get workflow details before checking history
automation_schedule_workflow - Set up recurring executions to monitor
automation_deactivate_workflow - Pause workflow if too many failures
automation_update_workflow - Fix workflow based on error patterns

Export workflow as JSON for backup, sharing, or import into another system.

- automation_id, slug, title, description, category
- trigger configuration (type, cron, event)
- actions array with tool names and parameters

}

You can save this JSON to a file or share it with others. To restore, use automation_import_workflow() (if available) or recreate with automation_create_workflow().'

tools.name: automation_open_workflow_in_canvas
tools.description:
Open a workflow in the visual automation canvas for the user to see and edit. Use this when user wants to view or edit a workflow visually (e.g., 'show me that workflow', 'open the email automation', 'let me see the workflow'). This switches the UI to the Automation tab and loads the workflow on the canvas.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this when user wants to SEE or EDIT workflow visually
- Switches UI to Automation tab automatically
- Loads workflow on drag-and-drop canvas with nodes and connections
- User can then modify workflow with visual editor
- Provide helpful message explaining what user will see

WHEN TO USE:
- User says 'show me the workflow', 'let me see it', 'open that automation'
- User wants to edit workflow ('I need to change the schedule', 'add another step')
- User wants visual representation ('what does it look like?')
- After creating workflow ('Here's your workflow, I'm opening it so you can see')

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'Opening your Daily Gmail Summary workflow in the visual editor...

I've switched to the Automation tab and loaded your workflow. You'll see:

🟢 Green hexagon: Schedule trigger (9:00 AM daily)
🔵 Blue rectangle: Get Gmail messages
🔵 Blue rectangle: Summarize with AI
🔵 Blue rectangle: Send email

You can now:
- Drag nodes to rearrange
- Click nodes to edit parameters
- Add new actions from the tools panel
- Connect nodes by dragging between ports
- Save changes when done'

UI ACTIONS:
1. Sends command to frontend: {type: 'open_automation_canvas', slug: 'wf_xxx'}
2. Frontend switches to Automation tab
3. Frontend loads workflow JSON (shapes, connections)
4. Frontend renders visual flowchart
5. User can interact with visual editor

PARAMETERS:
- slug='wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847' (required)
- message_to_user='Here is your workflow...' (optional, shown in UI)

message_to_user.description: Optional message to display to user when opening workflow (e.g., 'Here is your email automation workflow. You can edit it visually.')

returns.description: Confirmation that workflow was opened in canvas with UI command

tools.name: automation_publish_workflow
tools.description:
Publish a draft workflow as a live automation. Validates workflow structure, activates it for execution, optionally schedules it with cron expression, and links it to the current thread. Use this when user says 'publish this workflow', 'activate the automation', 'make this live', or 'schedule this to run'.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this after user finishes building workflow in canvas
- Validates workflow structure (has trigger, has actions, no errors)
- Changes status from 'draft' to 'active'
- Optionally creates schedule with cron expression
- Links workflow to current thread for easy access
- Returns validation results and next steps

VALIDATION CHECKS:
1. Workflow has at least one action
2. Trigger is properly configured
3. All tool names are valid (from 594 available tools)
4. Required parameters are present
5. Placeholder syntax is correct ({{variable}})
6. No circular dependencies

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'✓ Your Daily Gmail Summary workflow is now published!

**Validation:** All checks passed
**Status:** Active
**Workflow ID:** wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847
**Schedule:** Daily at 9:00 AM (UTC)
**Next Run:** Tomorrow at 9:00 AM
**Thread Link:** Added to this conversation

Your workflow will now:
1. Run automatically every morning at 9:00 AM
2. Get your unread Gmail messages
3. Generate an AI summary
4. Email you the digest

You can:
- View execution history: automation_get_execution_history()
- Pause schedule: automation_deactivate_workflow()
- Run manually: automation_execute_workflow()
- Edit in canvas: automation_open_workflow_in_canvas()'

PARAMETERS:
- slug='wf_xxx' (required, workflow to publish)
- thread_id=123 (optional, links to conversation)
- automation_title='My Workflow (Live)' (optional, custom name)
- schedule_cron='0 9 * * *' (optional, schedule)
- timezone='America/New_York' (optional, defaults to UTC)

WITHOUT SCHEDULING:
- If no schedule_cron provided, workflow is published as 'manual trigger only'
- User must run with automation_execute_workflow()
- Good for on-demand workflows or event-triggered workflows

thread_id.description: Thread ID to link the published automation to (usually the current thread)

automation_title.description: Optional custom title for the live automation (e.g., 'Email to Sheets (Production)'). If not provided, adds '(Live)' to workflow title.

schedule_cron.description: Optional cron expression for scheduling (e.g., '0 9 * * *' for daily at 9am, '0 */1 * * *' for hourly). If provided, automation will run on schedule.

timezone.description: Optional timezone for schedule (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'UTC'). Defaults to UTC.

returns.description: Publish result with validation status, automation_slug, scheduling info, and success message. Includes validation warnings/errors, next run time if scheduled, and thread linking confirmation.

examples.description: Publish workflow and schedule it to run hourly
Publish workflow without scheduling (manual execution only)

tools.name: automation_get_workflow_status
tools.description:
Get the current status of a workflow/automation including execution history, scheduling information, and success rate. Use this when user asks 'how is my workflow doing?', 'show me the status', 'is it running?', or 'when did it last run?'.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this for high-level workflow health check
- Returns summary of workflow performance and current state
- Shows scheduling info, execution stats, and last run details
- Simpler than automation_get_execution_history() (shows summary, not full logs)
- Good for quick status updates

RESPONSE INCLUDES:
**Metadata:**
- automation_id, slug, title, description, category
- status: 'draft', 'active', 'inactive'
- created_at, updated_at

**Scheduling:**
- schedule_cron (if scheduled)
- timezone
- next_run_time (ISO timestamp)
- is_scheduled (true/false)

**Execution Stats:**
- total_executions (all-time count)
- successful_executions (success count)
- failed_executions (failure count)
- success_rate (percentage)
- currently_running (true/false)

**Last Execution:**
- last_execution_id
- last_execution_time (ISO timestamp)
- last_execution_duration (seconds)
- last_execution_status ('success'/'failure')
- last_execution_error (if failed)

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'Here's the status of your Daily Gmail Summary workflow:

🟢 **Status:** Active and running
📅 **Schedule:** Daily at 9:00 AM (America/New_York)
⏰ **Next Run:** Tomorrow at 9:00 AM (in 14 hours)

📊 **Performance:**
- Total Executions: 45
- Success Rate: 95.6% (43 successful, 2 failed)
- Average Duration: 4.1 seconds

🕐 **Last Run:**
- Time: 2 hours ago (Today at 9:00 AM)
- Duration: 4.2 seconds
- Status: ✓ Success
- Result: Processed 8 emails, sent summary

Your workflow is healthy and running smoothly!'

WHEN TO USE:
- User asks 'is my workflow working?'
- Quick health check
- Monitor after recent changes
- Check if workflow is scheduled vs manual
- See when it will run next

VS automation_get_execution_history():
- use get_workflow_status() for SUMMARY
- use get_execution_history() for DETAILED LOGS

slug.description: Workflow slug to check status for (e.g., 'workflow-1737052800')

returns.description: Complete status information including workflow metadata (title, status, schedule), execution stats (total runs, success rate, currently running), and last execution details (time, duration, status, error if failed). Also includes next run time if scheduled.

examples.description: Check status of email automation
